questions.question: What does LDA assume about each document?
options: Each document belongs to exactly one topic — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Documents are sentences
Each document is a mixture of topics; each topic is a distribution over words
Documents are independent of topics
questions.explanation: LDA's generative story is mixed-membership: each doc has a topic distribution, each topic a word distribution.

questions.question: What does BERTopic use to form topic clusters?
options: Direct softmax over the vocabulary, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
Encode docs with a sentence transformer, reduce dimensionality with UMAP, then cluster with HDBSCAN
Run BM25 followed by k-means
Train an LSTM end-to-end
questions.explanation: BERTopic = embeddings + UMAP + HDBSCAN, with class-based TF-IDF for topic words.

questions.question: Why does scikit-learn's LDA expect raw counts (CountVectorizer), not TF-IDF?
options: TF-IDF is too slow
LDA's probabilistic model is defined over integer term counts; TF-IDF distorts the underlying distribution
LDA cannot handle floats, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
Memory limits
questions.explanation: LDA likelihood assumes counts; feeding TF-IDF values violates the model assumption.

questions.question: What does HDBSCAN's -1 label mean in a BERTopic output?
options: A reserved category, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
An outlier cluster of documents the density-based algorithm could not confidently assign
Stopword cluster
Top topic
questions.explanation: HDBSCAN marks unclustered points with -1; in BERTopic these are documents that did not fit any topic.

questions.question: Which coherence metric is the common default for topic-model evaluation?
options: BLEU
Accuracy
Perplexity only — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
c_v coherence via NPMI over sliding windows of top topic words
questions.explanation: c_v coherence (Roder et al., 2015) is the canonical automatic topic-coherence metric.

questions.question: When is LDA usually a better fit than BERTopic?
options: On short tweets
Long documents where mixed-membership topic distributions are useful and embeddings would truncate input
When embeddings are noisy
When you need a single topic per document, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: Long documents benefit from LDA's mixed-membership model; BERT encoders truncate inputs.
